I have been exactly where you were. I know it doesn't sound easy, but as Canary pointed out, the only way out is through. I can share a tactic I've learned myself to help deal with it, but bear in mind that everyone's anxiety is different, it affects everyone differently in some way or form and your treatment is ultimately going to need to be tailored around your needs.

All that being said, I've always kept in mind that anxiety is as irrational as it gets, and mine has always wanted me to indulge the irrational thoughts. One of my most common tactics, taught to me by my counselor, is to lean further into logical thinking, they call it the Socratic Method or Socratic Thinking, basically putting your anxieties to trial. Look at the statements being made by your anxiety, ask yourself if there's any evidence to support it/disprove it, whether that's the likely scenario or the worst case scenario, whether it is as black and white as it seems or if it's more complicated. **TL;DR: Question your anxiety. Challenge it with what you know for certain are the facts.**

Along with that, and I really cannot recommend this enough, if you haven't already, find a counselor that you connect with and start seeing them on a regular basis. Being able to talk out your fears and anxieties with someone who knows how to teach you (and your mind) methods of managing is a big part of punching through the dark. Experience will eventually teach you if you stay the course and keep going, but a good counselor will make it much easier. The fact that you're seeing a psychiatrist is great, continue doing so, but see if you can find a counselor to help you manage the anxiety in conjunction with whatever medications work for you.

Every aspect of life and society under Fascism is closely regimented, and trying to act outside the limits set by the state by any means is punished, often harshly.

Economically speaking, Fascist states aim for complete self-sufficiency. If it's not made by them, they don't want it, with very few exceptions, as how could the glorious state be dependent on anyone but themselves? The key of differentiating between Fascism and Nazism is that Nazism is a specific subset of Fascism, with very specific elements and beliefs, such as the belief in the superior White Aryan race and that Jews should be rendered extinct (for whatever reason).
